newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian religious leader questioned over riots.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian religious leader questioned over riots.

text.p: An Indonesian Moslem leader will be charged in connection with recent riots in the central Java town of Pekalongan, Antara news agency reported on Wednesday.
It said Afifudin Musytari was questioned for eight hours on Tuesday in Semarang, the capital of Central Java province, in connection with riots that rocked Pekalongan two weeks ago.
Sporadic clashes have recurred since then in the town, 300 km (190 miles) east of Jakarta.
Antara said Musytari, who runs an Islamic school in Pekalongan, was not arrested but was banned from preaching while the investigation was underway.

"According to police, the suspect will be charged with articles dealing with inciting riots and spreading hatred," said the agency. Antara gave no further details and police were not available for comment.

Violence broke out in Pekalongan, a stronghold of the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP), two weeks ago when PPP flags were removed by workers of the ruling Golkar party before a popular singer was to visit the area.
The singer used to campaign for the PPP but is now a Golkar candidate for the May 29 general elections.
Eight people were injured, at least 60 shops were burned or ransacked and a state-run bank was damaged during the violence, whose main target was the property of the ethnic chinese.
Thirty people have brought to court and have been imprisoned for between three days and three months for their involvement.
News that Musytari would be questioned in connection with the rioting sparked fresh violence last Sunday when a mob looted a motorcycle dealership near Pekalongan.
Troops were called out in the city early on Tuesday after hundreds of people -- apparently PPP supporters -- attacked a housing estate inhabited mostly by civil servants.
Civil servants usually support the ruling party. A number of motorcycles were burned during the violence and witnesses said two people were taken away by the police.
Residents said on Wednesday that troops were still stationed in many parts of the city, but tensions seemed to be easing.
"Troops are still being deployed in the city but residents seem to be calm," one resident told Reuters by telephone.

Antara quoted Religious Affairs Minister Tarmidzi Thaher on Sunday as saying there was evidence the Pekalongan rioting was triggered by a religious leader who lacked a "broad national insight". He did not explain the remark.
